sources.title: Hagerty Introduces Charles Kushner, Trump’s Nominee to be U.S. Ambassador to France and Monaco
highlights: —Today, United States Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and former U.S. Ambassador to Japan, introduced Charles “Charlie” Kushner, President Trump’s nominee to be U.S. Ambassador to France and Monaco. ... **Remarks as prepared for delivery:** Chairman Risch and Ranking Member Shaheen, thank you for holding this important nominations hearing today. It is my honor to introduce my good friend, Charles “Charlie” Kushner—President Trump’s nominee to be the U.S. Ambassador to France and Monaco. I have been fortunate to get to know Charlie, his wife Seryl and their wonderful family. ... who treats his employees like family, and a respected philanthropist. As a lifelong businessman who served as U.S. Ambassador to Japan during President Trump’s first term, I believe the ... ambassador in Paris. Yet President Trump selected Charlie for this role—not only because of his business acumen and experience in tough ... importance of our transatlantic relationships. Charlie understands the unique and enduring bond between the United States and France—a bond rooted in shared history, democratic values, and mutual interests. He is committed to advancing U.S. national security interests by deepening the U.S.-France alliance through pragmatic defense collaboration and fair, reciprocal trade relations. In short, Charlie is a do-er, and he’s energized not only to represent our country, but also accomplish things for the American people.I am confident that Charlie, when he is confirmed, will work tirelessly to build a more secure and prosperous future for both the American and French people.I look forward to his testimony today and to working with my colleagues on this committee to ensure his nomination moves forward as quickly as possible. ###

# Tracking Trump’s Cabinet picks Here's who has a seat at the table
By POLITICO Staff 11/12/2024 07:06 AM MST|Updated03/27/2025 01:09 PM MDT President Donald Trump is beginning to fill his Cabinet, the members of which will help implement his priorities. Despite concerns about the qualifications of some of Trump's Cabinet nominees, every single secretary position has now been filled and only a handful of Cabinet-level roles remain unconfirmed. Trump has withdrawn two nominees from ... for attorney general. The second was Rep. Elise Stefanik’s nomination to be United Nations ambassador amid worries about the House’s narrow GOP majority. The most controversial confirmation proved to be Pete Hegseth , who faced accusations of alcoholism, sexual assault and lack of experience. He lost the support of three Republican senators and was confirmed on Jan. 24 with a tie-breaking vote from Vice President JD Vance. This is POLITICO’s guide to Trump’s Cabinet picks including roles considered Cabinet-level in recent administrations. We’re tracking each of Trump’s choices, from selection to final floor vote below. ## Latest update
